page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 12 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory. The processing power is driven by an AMD EPYC 9575F CPU using the x86_64 architecture, featuring 12 physical cores with a single thread per core on a shared allocation model. Graphics and parallel processing acceleration are provided by two NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3942.28 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 42.79 GB/sec, placing both in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 45719.52 and Passmark CPU scoring 35206.69, both falling into the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth is also average, measuring 146.11 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 89.37 GB/sec for large block write operations. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 349.81 tokens/sec using a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing for the same model remains in the average tier at 1842.33 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by pairing two enterprise-grade NVIDIA L4 GPUs with a substantial 128.0 GB memory footprint, making it a viable configuration for GPU-bound tasks without paying for excessive CPU cores. However, the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs that require external storage integration and may introduce CPU performance variability under high neighbor load. This server is suited for workloads such as small-scale LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science tasks, and GPU-accelerated rendering.
